shloka_text: श्रुत्वा सेनापतिं प्राप्तं भरतं केकयाधिपः । युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं परां प्रीतिमुपागमत् ।। 7.101.1 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā senāpatiṃ prāptaṃ bharataṃ kekayādhipaḥ | yudhājidgārgyasahitaṃ parāṃ prītimupāgamat || 7.101.1 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, सेनापतिं the commander, प्राप्तं arrived, भरतं Bharata, केकयाधिपः the king of Kekaya, युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं accompanied by Yudhajit and Gargya, परां great, प्रीतिम् joy, उपागमत् attained.
explanation: Having heard that Commander Bharata had arrived, the King of Kekaya, accompanied by Yudhajit and Gargya, attained great joy.
comments: Bharata and Yudhajit reach the Gandharva city, and after a seven-night battle Bharata looses the dread Samvarta weapon of Time and slays three crore Gandharvas in an instant -- he founds two cities in Gandhara, Takshashila for Taksha and Pushkalavati for Pushkala, and after five years returns to report to Rama, who is pleased.

shloka_text: स निर्ययौ जनौघेन महता केकयाधिपः । त्वरमाणो ऽभिचक्राम गन्धर्वान्कामरूपिणः ।। 7.101.2 ।।
transliteration: sa niryayau janaughena mahatā kekayādhipaḥ | tvaramāṇo 'bhicakrāma gandharvānkāmarūpiṇaḥ || 7.101.2 ||
translation: सः he, निर्ययौ went out, जनौघेन with a multitude of people, महता great, केकयाधिपः the king of Kekaya, त्वरमाणो hurrying, अभिचक्राम approached, गन्धर्वान् the Gandharvas, कामरूपिणः who could change their form at will.
explanation: The King of Kekaya went out with a great multitude of people, hurrying to approach the Gandharvas who could change their form at will.

shloka_text: भरतश्च युधाजिच्च समेतौ लघुविक्रमैः । गन्धर्वनगरं प्राप्तौ सबलौ सपदानुगौ ।। 7.101.3 ।।
transliteration: bharataśca yudhājicca sametau laghuvikramaiḥ | gandharvanagaraṃ prāptau sabalau sapadānugau || 7.101.3 ||
translation: भरतश्च Bharata and, युधाजिच्च Yudhajit and, समेतौ together, लघुविक्रमैः with swift warriors, गन्धर्वनगरं to the city of the Gandharvas, प्राप्तौ arrived, सबलौ with their army, सपदानुगौ with their followers.
explanation: Bharata and Yudhajit, accompanied by swift warriors, arrived together at the city of the Gandharvas with their army and followers.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु भरतं प्राप्तं गन्धर्वास्ते समागताः । योद्धुकामा महावीर्या व्यनदन् वै समन्ततः ।। 7.101.4 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu bharataṃ prāptaṃ gandharvāste samāgatāḥ | yoddhukāmā mahāvīryā vyanadan vai samantataḥ || 7.101.4 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, भरतम् Bharata, प्राप्तम् arrived, गन्धर्वाः the Gandharvas, ते those, समागताः assembled, योद्धुकामाः desirous of fighting, महावीर्याः of great valor, व्यनदन् roared, वै indeed, समन्ततः all around.
explanation: Having heard of Bharata's arrival, those mighty Gandharvas, eager to fight, assembled and roared from all directions.

shloka_text: ततः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम् । सप्तरात्रं महाभीमं न चान्यतरयोर्जयः ।। 7.101.5 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam | saptarātraṃ mahābhīmaṃ na cānyatarayorjayaḥ || 7.101.5 ||
translation: ततः then, समभवत् occurred, युद्धम् a battle, तुमुलम् tumultuous, रोमहर्षणम् hair-raising, सप्तरात्रम् for seven nights, महाभीमम् exceedingly dreadful, न not, च and, अन्यतरयोः of either of the two, जयः victory.
explanation: Then, a tumultuous, hair-raising, and exceedingly dreadful battle ensued for seven nights, with neither side achieving victory.

shloka_text: खड्गशक्तिधनुर्ग्राहा नद्यः शोणितसंस्रवाः । नृकलेवरवाहिन्यः प्रवृत्ताः सर्वतोदिशम् ।। 7.101.6 ।।
transliteration: khaḍgaśaktidhanurgrāhā nadyaḥ śoṇitasaṃsravāḥ | nṛkalevaravāhinyaḥ pravṛttāḥ sarvatodiśam || 7.101.6 ||
translation: खड्ग swords, शक्ति spears, धनुः bows, ग्राहाः (like) alligators, नद्यः rivers, शोणित blood, संस्रवाः flowing, नृकलेवर human corpses, वाहिन्यः carrying, प्रवृत्ताः flowed, सर्वतोदिशम् in all directions.
explanation: Rivers of flowing blood, carrying human corpses and resembling streams with swords, spears, and bows as their aquatic creatures, flowed in all directions.

shloka_text: ततो रामानुजः क्रुद्धः कालस्यास्त्रं सुदारुणम् । संवर्तं नाम भरतो गन्धर्वेष्वभ्यचोदयत् ।। 7.101.7 ।।
transliteration: tato rāmānujaḥ kruddhaḥ kālasyāstraṃ sudāruṇam | saṃvartaṃ nāma bharato gandharveṣvabhyacodayat || 7.101.7 ||
translation: ततः then, रामानुजः Rama's younger brother, क्रुद्धः enraged, कालस्य of Time, अस्त्रम् weapon, सुदारुणम् exceedingly terrible, संवर्तम् Samvarta, नाम named, भरतः Bharata, गन्धर्वेषु upon the Gandharvas, अभ्यचोदयत् discharged.
explanation: Then, the enraged Bharata, Rama's younger brother, discharged the exceedingly terrible weapon of Time, named Samvarta, upon the Gandharvas.

shloka_text: ते बद्धाः कालपाशेन संवर्तेन विदारिताः । क्षणेनाभिहतास्तेन तिस्रः कोट्यो महात्मनाम् ।। 7.101.8 ।।
transliteration: te baddhāḥ kālapāśena saṃvartena vidāritāḥ | kṣaṇenābhihatāstena tisraḥ koṭyo mahātmanām || 7.101.8 ||
translation: ते they, बद्धाः bound, कालपाशेन by the noose of Time, संवर्तेन by Samvarta, विदारिताः torn apart, क्षणेन in a moment, अभिहताः struck down, तेन by him, तिस्रः three, कोट्यः crores, महात्मनाम् of mighty ones.
explanation: Bound by the noose of Time and torn apart by the Samvarta weapon, three crores of those mighty Gandharvas were instantly struck down by Bharata.

shloka_text: तं घातं घोरसङ्काशं न स्मरन्ति दिवौकसः । निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तादृशानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.101.9 ।।
transliteration: taṃ ghātaṃ ghorasaṅkāśaṃ na smaranti divaukasaḥ | nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tādṛśānāṃ mahātmanām || 7.101.9 ||
translation: तं that, घातं destruction, घोरसङ्काशं terrible-looking, न not, स्मरन्ति remember, दिवौकसः gods, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण within the mere twinkling of an eye, तादृशानाम् of such, महात्मनाम् great souls.
explanation: The gods do not even remember that terrible destruction of those great souls (Gandharvas), as it occurred within the mere twinkling of an eye.

shloka_text: हतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु भरतः केकयीसुतः । निवेशयामास तदा समृद्धे द्वे पुरोत्तमे ।। 7.101.10 ।।
transliteration: hateṣu teṣu sarveṣu bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ | niveśayāmāsa tadā samṛddhe dve purottame || 7.101.10 ||
translation: हतेषु having been killed, तेषु those, सर्वेषु all, भरतः Bharata, केकयीसुतः son of Kaikeyi, निवेशयामास established, तदा then, समृद्धे prosperous, द्वे two, पुरोत्तमे excellent cities.
explanation: After all those (Gandharvas) were killed, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi, then established two prosperous and excellent cities.

shloka_text: तक्षं तक्षशिलायां तु पुष्कलं पुष्कलावते । गन्धर्वदेशे रुचिरे गान्धारविषये च सः ।। 7.101.11 ।।
transliteration: takṣaṃ takṣaśilāyāṃ tu puṣkalaṃ puṣkalāvate | gandharvadeśe rucire gāndhāraviṣaye ca saḥ || 7.101.11 ||
translation: तक्षं Taksha (son of Bharata), तक्षशिलायां in Takshashila, तु and, पुष्कलम् Pushkala (son of Bharata), पुष्कलावते in Pushkalavati, गन्धर्वदेशे in the land of Gandharvas, रुचिरे beautiful, गान्धारविषये in the region of Gandhara, च and, सः he (Bharata).
explanation: He (Bharata) established Taksha in Takshashila and Pushkala in Pushkalavati, both in the beautiful land of Gandharvas, which is the region of Gandhara.

translation: धनरत्नौघसङ्कीर्णे filled with heaps of wealth and jewels, काननैरुपशोभिते adorned with forests, अन्योन्यसङ्घर्षकृते causing mutual rivalry, स्पर्धया with competition, गुणविस्तरैः with extensive qualities.
explanation: These cities were filled with heaps of wealth and jewels, adorned with forests, and their extensive qualities caused mutual rivalry and competition.

translation: उभे both, सुरुचिरप्रख्ये very beautiful in appearance, व्यवहारैरकिल्बिषैः with blameless transactions, उद्यानयानसम्पूर्णे full of gardens and conveyances, सुविभक्तान्तरापणे with well-divided inner markets.
explanation: Both cities were very beautiful in appearance, characterized by blameless transactions, full of gardens and conveyances, and had well-divided inner markets.

shloka_text: उभे पुरवरे रम्ये विस्तरैरुपशोभिते । गृहमुख्यैः सुरुचिरैर्विमानसमवर्णिभिः ।। 7.101.14 ।।
transliteration: ubhe puravare ramye vistarairupaśobhite | gṛhamukhyaiḥ surucirairvimānasamavarṇibhiḥ || 7.101.14 ||
translation: उभे both, पुरवरे excellent cities, रम्ये beautiful, विस्तरैः with extensive areas, उपशोभिते adorned, गृहमुख्यैः with principal houses, सुरुचिरैः very charming, विमानसमवर्णिभिः resembling celestial chariots in appearance.
explanation: Both beautiful and excellent cities were adorned with extensive areas, featuring principal houses that were very charming and resembled celestial chariots.

translation: शोभिते adorned, शोभनीयैः with beautiful ones, च and, देवायतनविस्तरैः with extensive temples, तालैः with palm trees, तमालैः with tamala trees, तिलकैर with tilaka trees, वकुलैः with vakula trees, उपशोभिते adorned.
explanation: The cities were further adorned with beautiful and extensive temples, as well as with palm, tamala, tilaka, and vakula trees.

translation: निवेश्य having established, पञ्चभिः by five, वर्षैः years, भरतः Bharata, राघवानुजः Rama's younger brother, पुनरायात् returned, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, केकयीसुतः Kaikeyi's son.
explanation: After establishing the cities over a period of five years, Bharata, the mighty-armed son of Kaikeyi and younger brother of Rama, returned to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं साक्षाद्धर्ममिवापरम् । राघवं भरतः श्रीमान्ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः ।। 7.101.17 ।।
transliteration: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ sākṣāddharmamivāparam | rāghavaṃ bharataḥ śrīmānbrahmāṇamiva vāsavaḥ || 7.101.17 ||
translation: सः he, अभिवाद्य having saluted, महात्मानम् the great-souled one, साक्षात् directly, धर्मम् Dharma, इव like, अपरम् another, राघवम् Rama, भरतः Bharata, श्रीमान् the glorious, ब्रह्माणम् Brahma, इव like, वासवः Indra.
explanation: The glorious Bharata, like Indra saluting Brahma, saluted the great-souled Rama, who was like another embodiment of Dharma itself.

shloka_text: शशंस च यथावृत्तं गन्धर्ववधमुत्तमम् । निवेशनं च देशस्य श्रुत्वा प्रीतो ऽस्य राघवः ।। 7.101.18 ।।
transliteration: śaśaṃsa ca yathāvṛttaṃ gandharvavadhamuttamam | niveśanaṃ ca deśasya śrutvā prīto 'sya rāghavaḥ || 7.101.18 ||
translation: शशंस he reported, च and, यथावृत्तम् the full account, गन्धर्ववधम् the slaying of the Gandharvas, उत्तमम् excellent, निवेशनम् the establishment, च and, देशस्य of the region, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रीतः pleased, अस्य his, राघवः Rama.
explanation: Bharata reported the full account of the excellent slaying of the Gandharvas and the establishment of the region, and upon hearing this, Rama was pleased with him. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 101 ।। Thus ends the hundred and first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
